note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in OK.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Talimena National Scenic Byway
byways.designation: National Scenic Byway (also an Oklahoma State Scenic Byway and a National Forest Scenic Byway)
byways.where: OK-1 from US-271 near Talihina east to the Arkansas line, continuing as AR-88 to Mena; Le Flore County

facts.fact: The drive runs 54 miles along the crest of Rich Mountain and Winding Stair Mountain between Mena, Arkansas, and Talihina, Oklahoma.
Along the way are Queen Wilhelmina State Park and the Robert S. Kerr Memorial Arboretum and Nature Center.
The route begins near Talimena State Park at Talihina, runs through the Ouachita National Forest and has scenic turnouts such as Castle Rock and Sugarloaf.

byways.name: Mountain Pass Scenic Byway
byways.where: US-259 between Page and Octavia, Le Flore County

facts.fact: The byway follows Highway 259 for 23 miles between Page and Octavia.
It crosses the tops of the Ouachita Mountains and passes through the 26,445-acre Winding Stair Mountain National Recreation Area, with the Kerr Arboretum nearby.
Both Mountain Pass and Mountain Gateway are two-lane paved roads with steep hills and curves reaching nearly 2,600 feet.

byways.name: Mountain Gateway Scenic Byway
byways.where: US-59/270 from Heavener to the Arkansas line, Le Flore County

facts.fact: The byway follows Highway 59/270 for 22 miles between Heavener and the Arkansas state line.
It winds through forested valleys of the Ouachita Mountains and the Winding Stair Mountain National Recreation Area, with steep grades and sharp curves.
Wildflowers bloom along it in spring and the forest colors in autumn.

byways.name: Route 66
byways.designation: National Scenic Byway and All-American Road
byways.where: Old US-66 across Oklahoma from Quapaw to Texola, via Miami, Tulsa, Oklahoma City and Calumet

facts.fact: Route 66 covers nearly 400 miles in Oklahoma, from Quapaw to Texola.
Stops include the Will Rogers Memorial Museum in Claremore and the Coleman Theatre in Miami, with its Wurlitzer organ.
Oklahoma has the nation's longest driveable stretch of Route 66.

byways.name: Osage Nation Heritage Trail
byways.where: US-60 from Ponca City east through Pawhuska to Bartlesville; Kay, Osage and Washington counties

facts.fact: The trail follows Highway 60 from Ponca City east through Pawhuska to Bartlesville, through the Osage Hills.
Nearby are the Tallgrass Prairie Preserve and the estates of oil men such as Frank Phillips and E. W. Marland.
Pawhuska is the Osage Nation capital, and its Osage Nation Museum is known as the oldest tribally owned museum in the United States.

byways.name: Cherokee Hills Scenic Byway
byways.designation: National Scenic Byway (also an Oklahoma State Scenic Byway)
byways.where: SH-10 north of I-40 in Sequoyah County via Gore, SH-100 and SH-82 to Tahlequah, then SH-10 north and US-59/412 Alt to West Siloam Springs

facts.fact: The route runs 84 miles from Highway 10 north of I-40 in Sequoyah County through Gore, Cookson and Tahlequah to the Arkansas line at West Siloam Springs.
It passes Lake Tenkiller, the Cookson Hills and Tahlequah, the Cherokee Nation capital, then runs beside the Illinois River.
Natural Falls State Park on the northern part of the route has the tallest waterfall in Oklahoma.

byways.name: Wichita Mountains Scenic Byway
byways.designation: National Scenic Byway (also an Oklahoma State Scenic Byway)
byways.where: Loop west of Apache on SH-19, 58, 9, 115 and 49 via Carnegie, Mountain View and Medicine Park, through the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge; Comanche, Caddo and Kiowa counties

facts.fact: The byway begins at Apache and follows Highways 19, 58, 9, 115 and 49, reaching Carnegie, Mountain View and Medicine Park and running through the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge.
The country is a mix of rocky lowlands, mixed-grass prairie and cross timbers, and the refuge is home to bison.
Bison graze the refuge below Mount Scott, and Medicine Park is a cobblestone town near Bath Lake.

byways.name: Kenton to Keys State Scenic Byway
byways.where: SH-325 from the New Mexico line through Kenton to Boise City, then US-56/US-64 east toward Keyes (to SH-171); Cimarron County

facts.fact: ODOT's scenic byway layer describes this State Scenic Byway as SH-325 from the New Mexico state line east to US-56, then US-56 and US-64 to SH-171.
SH-325 runs from the New Mexico border through Kenton to Boise City and gives access to Black Mesa State Park near Black Mesa.
Kenton sits among mesas formed by ancient lava flows and is the only Oklahoma town on Mountain Standard Time; Black Mesa, the state's highest point at 4,973 feet, rises east of town.

byways.review: Not in the catalog. The state's name spells 'Keys'; the town is Keyes. Not on the TravelOK byways article and the url is the TravelOK Kenton town page because no byway page exists. The Oklahoma Commerce layer's PDFMap link for this byway wrongly points to the Mountain Pass listing.

issues: No ODOT program page or official register was found; the list of eight (four national, four state) comes from TravelOK's article, which counts 'four State Scenic Byways' but names only three; the fourth, Kenton to Keys, comes from the ODOT and Commerce GIS layers.

ODOT's billboard-control layer has more lines than the eight program byways: 'State Scenic Route' segments B, F, H, I, K, N, Q (e.g. US-412 Gloss Mountains area, US-412/US-59 near Siloam Springs, roads around Talihina, SH-259A Beavers Bend loop, US-77 Arbuckles), plus M (SH-77 Arbuckle Mountains / Turner Falls area) typed 'State Scenic Byway' and O (SH-77 scenic loop) and R (US-283 SH-19 to SH-44) typed 'National Scenic Byway'. None of these appear in TravelOK or the FHWA list; M, O and R look like either old designations or mislabeled TYPE values. Worth a check with ODOT if more state byways exist.

Statutory memorial names that sound like byways but are not program members: 'Scenic U.S. Highway 412' (69 O.S. 1620), 'Mountain Gateway' covering US-59/271/259 in Le Flore County (69 O.S. 1634, broader than the Mountain Gateway Scenic Byway), 'Southeastern Mountain Gateway' SH-3 at Tom (69 O.S. 1650), 'Duty Rowe Scenic Route 115' (69 O.S. 1698.32).

Wichita Mountains catalog line is 105 mi; Oklahoma Commerce gives 93 mi. ODOT segment R (US-283 toward Quartz Mountain) is typed National Scenic Byway but is not in TravelOK's route description; check whether the catalog line includes it.

TravelOK gives Mountain Pass as 23 mi and Mountain Gateway as 22 mi; catalog has 24 and 23. ODOT's segment J (US-259 from SH-144 north, US-59 and SH-128 to the AR line) does not match either TravelOK description cleanly; check the catalog lines for Mountain Pass and Mountain Gateway against TravelOK (US-259 Page to Octavia; US-59/270 Heavener to the AR line).
Kenton to Keys is not drawn in the catalog; draw it from ODOT NAME='A'. Its eastern end in ODOT is US-64 at SH-171, about 3 miles south of Keyes.
